topics.t: Ethiopia polio campaign and community immunity gaps
topics.news: Ethiopia launched a polio vaccination campaign on 21 November 2026 after cases of circulating variant poliovirus type 1 in 2026, aiming to reach more than 11.3 million children. The first round runs from 21 to 24 November, with another round in December. The country remains free of wild poliovirus.

rows: Poliomyelitis
A vaccine-preventable disease that can cause paralysis, mainly in children.
Wild poliovirus
The naturally circulating virus; only Afghanistan and Pakistan still report it.
Circulating variant poliovirus
A form that arises from the weakened virus in the oral vaccine, when it spreads and mutates in under-immunised communities.
Surveillance
Acute flaccid paralysis surveillance and testing of sewage (environmental surveillance) detect the virus.
India
Declared polio-free by the World Health Organization in March 2014 after three years without a case.

ul: **Target:** 11.3 million children is the launch target, not coverage achieved.
**Lesson:** high routine immunisation and surveillance are needed to keep a region polio-free.

prel.d: A vaccine-derived virus that spreads where immunity is low.
Sudden weakness in a limb that is investigated to detect polio.

qs.q: India has been polio-free since 2014. Why must it remain vigilant?

topics.t: NCG VISHWAS: education and continuity in cancer care
topics.news: The Health Ministry launched NCG VISHWAS in Mumbai on 21 November 2026: AI-enabled, clinician-reviewed educational videos on breast, cervical and oral cancers, in Hindi, Marathi, Tamil and English, covering prevention, diagnosis, treatment and long-term care. The Ministry urged consent-based record linkage through ABHA and wider sharing through health workers and digital platforms.

rows: NCG
National Cancer Grid, a network of cancer centres and institutions across India.
ABHA
Ayushman Bharat Health Account, a digital health ID that allows consent-based linking of health records.
AB PM-JAY
Provides health coverage to eligible families under its own rules; an ABHA number alone does not make a person eligible.
Cancers covered
Breast, cervical and oral cancers, which are common and can be detected early by screening.

ul: **Why it matters:** late detection is a major reason for poor outcomes; education, screening and referral need to be linked.

prel.d: A network of cancer hospitals, research institutions and patient groups.
A health account number used to link a person’s health records with consent.

qs.q: Discuss the role of digital health initiatives in improving cancer prevention and care in India.

topics.t: Eastern Ghats landslides and rainfall-triggered slope failure
topics.news: Odisha has had 92 landslides across six districts so far in 2026. Destructive landslides on 28 October in Ganjam and Kandhamal damaged roads and isolated settlements.

rows: Pore-water pressure
Rainwater raises water pressure within soil, which lowers the effective stress and the resistance to sliding.
Terrain
Slope, geology and drainage decide how a hillside responds to rain.
Susceptibility, exposure, vulnerability
Three distinct parts of risk: how likely the slope is to fail, what lies in its path, and how badly people and property would be affected.
Mitigation
Intercepting surface water and removing sub-surface water through drains; avoiding cuts and construction on unstable slopes.

ul: **Eastern Ghats:** a discontinuous range along the east coast, less prone than the Himalaya but affected by heavy rain and road cutting.
**Impact:** road disruption increases the consequences by isolating settlements.

prel.d: Downslope movement of rock, soil or debris.
Pressure of water held in the spaces between soil particles.

qs.q: Explain the causes of landslides and the measures for their mitigation in India.

topics.t: Biosafety Level-4 laboratory planned at Bhopal
topics.news: Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan announced the construction of a Biosafety Level-4 laboratory at the ICAR-National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases, Bhopal.

rows: BSL-1 and BSL-2
Work on agents that pose low or moderate risk.
BSL-3
Work on agents that can cause serious disease through the air, with controlled access and special ventilation.
BSL-4
The highest level; for dangerous agents with no or limited treatment, such as Ebola and Nipah virus, with full-body suits and sealed facilities.
Use
Research on emerging animal diseases that can pass to humans, which is important for livestock and public health.

ul: **One Health:** human, animal and environmental health are linked, so animal disease laboratories matter for human health too.

prel.d: The highest containment level for work with the most dangerous pathogens.
An approach that treats human, animal and environmental health together.

qs.q: What is the One Health approach and why is it important for India?
